fields.name: GPIOR
fields.text: Free byte for software use, such as flags or variables, in bit-addressable I/O space.

fields.name: DEVICEID
fields.text: Byte n of the three-byte device ID (SIGROW.DEVICEID[2:0]), which tells software the device and its properties: memory sizes, pin count, die revision.

fields.name: SERNUM
fields.text: Byte n of the ten-byte serial number (SIGROW.SERNUM[9:0]), unique to each device.

fields.name: TEMPSENSE
fields.text: Byte n of the factory correction for the on-chip temperature sensor: TEMPSENSE0 corrects gain/slope (unsigned), TEMPSENSE1 corrects offset (signed); used with ADC temperature readings.

fields.name: OSC16ERR3V
fields.text: Signed frequency error of the internal oscillator against nominal, at 16 MHz and 3V, measured in production.

fields.name: OSC16ERR5V
fields.text: Signed frequency error of the internal oscillator against nominal, at 16 MHz and 5V, measured in production.

fields.name: OSC20ERR3V
fields.text: Signed frequency error of the internal oscillator against nominal, at 20 MHz and 3V, measured in production.

fields.name: OSC20ERR5V
fields.text: Signed frequency error of the internal oscillator against nominal, at 20 MHz and 5V, measured in production.

fields.name: WINDOW
fields.text: Copied into WDT.CTRLA.WINDOW at Reset: the watchdog window time-out period.

fields.name: PERIOD
fields.text: Copied into WDT.CTRLA.PERIOD at Reset: the watchdog time-out period.

fields.name: LVL
fields.text: Copied into BOD.CTRLB.LVL at Reset: the BOD threshold. Voltages given are typical.

fields.name: SAMPFREQ
fields.text: Copied into BOD.CTRLA.SAMPFREQ at Reset: how often the BOD samples.

fields.name: ACTIVE
fields.text: Copied into BOD.CTRLA.ACTIVE at Reset: the BOD mode in Active and Idle.

values.text: On; wake-up waits until the BOD is ready.

fields.name: SLEEP
fields.text: Copied into BOD.CTRLA.SLEEP at Reset: the BOD mode in sleep.

fields.name: OSCLOCK
fields.text: Copied into CLKCTRL.OSC20MCALIBB.LOCK at Reset: locks the OSC20M calibration registers.

values.text: OSC20M calibration registers can be accessed.

fields.name: FREQSEL
fields.text: Picks the OSC20M frequency, 16 or 20 MHz, and with it which factory calibration goes into CLKCTRL.OSC20MCALIBA.CAL20M and CLKCTRL.OSC20MCALIBB.TEMPCAL20M.

fields.name: CMPDEN
fields.text: Compare D enable.

fields.name: CMPCEN
fields.text: Compare C enable.

fields.name: CMPBEN
fields.text: Compare B enable.

fields.name: CMPAEN
fields.text: Compare A enable.

fields.name: CMPD
fields.text: State Compare D takes after Reset, and on entering debug when FAULTDET is '1'.

fields.name: CMPC
fields.text: State Compare C takes after Reset, and on entering debug when FAULTDET is '1'.

fields.name: CMPB
fields.text: State Compare B takes after Reset, and on entering debug when FAULTDET is '1'.

fields.name: CMPA
fields.text: State Compare A takes after Reset, and on entering debug when FAULTDET is '1'.

fields.name: CRCSRC
fields.text: Which Flash region gets a CRC check.

values.name: FLASH
values.text: Whole Flash: boot, application code and application data.

fields.name: RSTPINCFG
fields.text: Function of the Reset/UPDI pin. When it is set as GPIO, the pin's output driver stays off for 768 OSC32K cycles after a System Reset, so it cannot fight a high-voltage UPDI enable sequence; enable this pin's interrupts only after that time.

fields.name: EESAVE
fields.text: Keeps the EEPROM through a chip erase. A locked device has its EEPROM erased by a chip erase whatever this bit says.

fields.name: SUT
fields.text: Time from power-on until code starts running.

fields.name: APPEND
fields.text: End of the application code section, in 256-byte blocks, counted as boot size plus application code size; Flash past it is application data. 0x00 makes everything from BOOTEND*256 to the top of Flash application code. With FUSE.APPEND and FUSE.BOOTEND both 0x00, all of Flash is BOOT.

fields.name: BOOTEND
fields.text: End of the boot section, in 256-byte blocks. At 0x00 the whole Flash is the BOOT section, as it also is whenever FUSE.APPEND and FUSE.BOOTEND are both 0x00.

fields.name: LOCKBIT
fields.text: Memory lock key. While locked, UPDI has no system bus access and can read only the System Information Block (SIB).

values.text: Any other value: memory access locked.

fields.name: REVID
fields.text: Silicon revision, read-only: 0x00 is rev A, 0x01 rev B, counting up.

fields.name: CCP
fields.text: Write a signature here to open a four-instruction window for changing protected I/O registers or running protected instructions; interrupts are held off during the window and served afterwards by level and priority. Bit 0 reads 1 while the I/O-register unlock is active, bit 1 reads 1 while the self-programming unlock is active; bits 7:2 read 0.

registers.name: SP
registers.title: Stack Pointer
notes: After reset SP holds the highest internal SRAM address. Only as many bits as the data memory needs are implemented; the rest read 0. SPL holds bits 7:0 at the register offset, SPH bits 15:8 at offset + 0x01. Writing CPU.SPL holds off interrupts for four instructions, or less if an I/O memory write comes sooner.

fields.name: SP
fields.text: 16-bit stack pointer; the high byte holds the upper eight bits.

fields.name: I
fields.text: Global interrupt enable: 1 lets interrupts run, 0 blocks all of them whatever the peripheral enables say. Hardware does not clear it on ISR entry nor set it on RETI; SEI and CLI set and clear it. Writing it through the I/O register costs one wait cycle.

fields.name: T
fields.text: Bit store and bit load (BST, BLD) use T as the destination or source bit.

fields.name: H
fields.text: Set by a half carry in arithmetic that tracks it, cleared otherwise; used in BCD arithmetic.

fields.name: S
fields.text: Always N exclusive-or V.

fields.name: V
fields.text: Set by a two's complement overflow in arithmetic that tracks it, cleared otherwise.

fields.name: N
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic result is negative, cleared otherwise.

fields.name: Z
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic result is zero, cleared otherwise.

fields.name: C
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic operation carries, cleared otherwise.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Issues an NVM command when written. The SPM key must go to CCP no more than four instructions earlier.

values.name: WP
values.text: Write the page buffer to the memory NVMCTRL.ADDR points into.

values.name: ER
values.text: Erase the page in the memory NVMCTRL.ADDR points into.

values.name: ERWP
values.text: Erase, then write, the page in the memory NVMCTRL.ADDR points into.

values.name: CHER
values.text: Chip erase: Flash and EEPROM, EEPROM kept when FUSE.SYSCFG.EESAVE is 1.

fields.name: BOOTLOCK
fields.text: 1 blocks reads and instruction fetches from the boot section: both return 0. Writable only from the boot section, cleared only by a reset, and active from the first exit from the boot section after it is written.

fields.name: APCWP
fields.text: 1 write-protects the application code section. It can only be set; only a reset clears it.

fields.name: WRERROR
fields.text: Reads 1 after a write error in the last operation, such as writing to more than one section before a page write, or writing a protected area.

fields.name: EEBUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 while the EEPROM is busy with a command.

fields.name: FBUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 while the Flash is busy with a command.

fields.name: EEREADY
fields.text: 1 enables the EEPROM-ready interrupt, a level interrupt that fires while the EEREADY flag is 0. EEREADY is not set until an issued NVM command, so enable it only after starting the command; the handler may disable it.

fields.name: EEREADY
fields.text: Held set for as long as the EEPROM is idle; writing 1 clears it.

registers.name: DATA
registers.title: Data
notes: DATAL holds bits 7:0 at the register offset, DATAH bits 15:8 at offset + 0x01.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Data the UPDI uses when writing fuses.

registers.name: ADDR
registers.title: Address
notes: ADDRL holds bits 7:0 at the register offset, ADDRH bits 15:8 at offset + 0x01.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Address of the memory location written most recently.

fields.name: CLKOUT
fields.text: 1 puts the system clock on the CLKOUT pin, which exists on parts with 20 or more pins. During sleep the pin is silent except while some peripheral runs from the system clock.

fields.name: CLKSEL
fields.text: Source of the main clock, CLK_MAIN.

fields.name: PDIV
fields.text: Main clock prescaler ratio, used when PEN is 1; it may be changed while running. Software must keep CLK_PER within its maximum for the CLK_MAIN in use.

fields.name: PEN
fields.text: 1 turns the prescaler on with the ratio in PDIV; 0 passes the main clock straight through (CLK_PER = CLK_MAIN) whatever PDIV holds.

fields.name: LOCKEN
fields.text: 1 freezes CLKCTRL.MCLKCTRLA, CLKCTRL.MCLKCTRLB and, where there is one, the active main clock source's calibration against software writes; MCLKLOCK itself is then closed until the next hardware reset. Reset loads it from FUSE.OSCCFG.OSCLOCK.

fields.name: EXTS
fields.text: Whether the external clock has started.

fields.name: XOSC32KS
fields.text: Whether XOSC32K is stable. Valid only while the main clock or a peripheral requests the oscillator; with RUNSTDBY set but no request it reads 0.

fields.name: OSC32KS
fields.text: Whether OSCULP32K is stable. Valid only while the main clock or a peripheral requests the oscillator; with RUNSTDBY set but no request it reads 0.

fields.name: OSC20MS
fields.text: Whether OSC20M is stable. Valid only while the main clock or a peripheral requests the oscillator; with RUNSTDBY set but no request it reads 0.

fields.name: SOSC
fields.text: Shows a main clock source switch in progress.

values.text: Switching; CLK_MAIN moves to the new source once it is stable.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: 1 keeps the oscillator running in every mode even when nothing uses it, so a wake from Standby skips its start-up time. Its output still goes out only on request; a request opens the clock gate after four oscillator cycles.

fields.name: CAL20M
fields.text: Fine-tunes the OSC20M frequency around its centre value. Reset loads the factory value for the FUSE.OSCCFG.FREQSEL setting.

fields.name: LOCK
fields.text: When set, CLKCTRL.OSC20MCALIBA and CLKCTRL.OSC20MCALIBB cannot be changed. Reset loads it from FUSE.OSCCFG.OSCLOCK.

fields.name: TEMPCAL20M
fields.text: Adjusts the slope of the oscillator's temperature compensation. Reset loads the factory value for the FUSE.OSCCFG.FREQSEL setting.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: 1 keeps the oscillator running in every mode even when nothing uses it, so a wake from Standby skips its start-up time. Its output still goes out only on request; a request opens the clock gate after four oscillator cycles.

registers.name: XOSC32KCTRLA
registers.title: 32.768 kHz Crystal Oscillator Control A
notes: SEL and CSUT are locked while ENABLE is 1 or CLKCTRL.MCLKSTATUS.XOSC32KS is 1; to change them, clear ENABLE, wait for XOSC32KS to read 0, then enable again.

fields.name: CSUT
fields.text: Start-up time of XOSC32K. Locked while ENABLE is 1, and not used when SEL is 1.

fields.name: SEL
fields.text: Kind of external source. Locked while ENABLE is 1.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: With ENABLE set, 1 starts the crystal oscillator and keeps it running in Active, Idle and Standby even when unused, so once its first start-up is done a request gets the clock after two to three cycles. At 0 it runs only while requested and enabled. Its output reaches peripherals only when they request it. The bit is I/O protected.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: 1 hands the TOSC1 and TOSC2 pins to the oscillator and makes SEL and CSUT read-only. The bit is I/O protected.

fields.name: SMODE
fields.text: Sleep mode entered by SLEEP while SEN is 1.

fields.name: SEN
fields.text: Must be 1 for the SLEEP instruction to put the MCU into the mode in SMODE.

registers.name: RSTFR
registers.title: Reset Flag Register
notes: Each flag clears on a write of 1. A power-on reset clears all of them except PORF.

fields.name: UPDIRF
fields.text: Set by a UPDI reset.

fields.name: SWRF
fields.text: Set by a software reset.

fields.name: WDRF
fields.text: Set by a watchdog reset.

fields.name: EXTRF
fields.text: Set by an external reset.

fields.name: BORF
fields.text: Set by a brown-out reset.

fields.name: PORF
fields.text: Set by a power-on reset, which clears every other flag; none of the others can be set until a full boot after the POR has run.

fields.name: SWRE
fields.text: Writing 1 resets the device by software. Always reads 0.

fields.name: IVSEL
fields.text: Where the interrupt vectors sit. Protected by CCP.

fields.name: CVT
fields.text: Turns the compact vector table on. Protected by CCP.

fields.name: LVL0RR
fields.text: Round-robin priority for level 0 interrupts. Not protected by CCP.

values.text: Fixed priority: the lowest vector address wins.

fields.name: NMIEX
fields.text: Set while a non-maskable interrupt runs; cleared by RETI from its handler.

fields.name: LVL1EX
fields.text: Set while a level 1 interrupt runs, including when an NMI has interrupted its handler; cleared by RETI from the handler.

fields.name: LVL0EX
fields.text: Set while a level 0 interrupt runs, including when a level 1 interrupt or an NMI has interrupted its handler; cleared by RETI from the handler.

fields.name: LVL0PRI
fields.text: Changes the priority order of level 0 interrupts.

fields.name: LVL1VEC
fields.text: Number of the one vector raised to priority level 1; 0x00 means no vector, so level 1 is off.

fields.name: ASYNCSTROBE
fields.text: A write inverts each event channel for one system clock cycle, producing one event.

fields.name: SYNCSTROBE
fields.text: A write inverts each event channel for one system clock cycle, producing one event.

fields.name: ASYNCCH
fields.text: Picks the event generator for asynchronous channel n. Parts with fewer pins lack some port pins.

fields.name: SYNCCH
fields.text: Picks the event generator for synchronous channel n. Parts with fewer pins lack some port pins.

registers.name: ASYNCUSERn
registers.title: Asynchronous User Channel n Input Selection

fields.name: ASYNCUSER
fields.text: Channel feeding asynchronous user n. Users 0 to 12: TCB0, ADC0, CCL LUT0 event 0, CCL LUT1 event 0, CCL LUT0 event 1, CCL LUT1 event 1, TCD0 event 0, TCD0 event 1, EVOUT0, EVOUT1, EVOUT2, TCB1, ADC1.

registers.name: SYNCUSERn
registers.title: Synchronous User Channel n Input Selection

fields.name: SYNCUSER
fields.text: Channel feeding synchronous user n. User 0 is TCA0, user 1 is USART0.

fields.name: LUT1
fields.text: 1 moves the CCL LUT1 output to its alternative pin.

fields.name: LUT0
fields.text: 1 moves the CCL LUT0 output to its alternative pin.

fields.name: EVOUT2
fields.text: 1 turns on event output 2.

fields.name: EVOUT1
fields.text: 1 turns on event output 1.

fields.name: EVOUT0
fields.text: 1 turns on event output 0.

fields.name: TWI0
fields.text: 1 moves TWI0 to its alternative pins.

fields.name: SPI0
fields.text: 1 moves SPI0 to its alternative pins.

fields.name: USART0
fields.text: 1 moves USART0 to its alternative pins.

fields.name: TCA05
fields.text: 1 moves TCA0 waveform output 5 to its alternative pin; Split mode only, no effect in Normal mode.

fields.name: TCA04
fields.text: 1 moves TCA0 waveform output 4 to its alternative pin; Split mode only, no effect in Normal mode.

fields.name: TCA03
fields.text: 1 moves TCA0 waveform output 3 to its alternative pin; Split mode only, no effect in Normal mode.

fields.name: TCA02
fields.text: 1 moves TCA0 waveform output 2 to its alternative pin; in Split mode it governs the low-byte compare channel 2 output.

fields.name: TCA01
fields.text: 1 moves TCA0 waveform output 1 to its alternative pin; in Split mode it governs the low-byte compare channel 1 output.

fields.name: TCA00
fields.text: 1 moves TCA0 waveform output 0 to its alternative pin; in Split mode it governs the low-byte compare channel 0 output.

fields.name: TCB1
fields.text: 1 moves the TCB1 output to its alternative pin.

fields.name: TCB0
fields.text: 1 moves the TCB0 output to its alternative pin.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: One bit per pin turning its output driver on or off; the digital input buffer is set by ISC in PORTx.PINnCTRL, not here.

fields.name: DIRSET
fields.text: Writing 1 to bit n sets PORTx.DIR bit n, making Pxn an output; 0 does nothing. Reads return PORTx.DIR.

fields.name: DIRCLR
fields.text: Writing 1 to bit n clears PORTx.DIR bit n, making Pxn input only; 0 does nothing. Reads return PORTx.DIR.

fields.name: DIRTGL
fields.text: Writing 1 to bit n flips PORTx.DIR bit n; 0 does nothing. Reads return PORTx.DIR.

fields.name: OUT
fields.text: One bit per pin giving its output level; matters only where PORTx.DIR has the driver on.

fields.name: OUTSET
fields.text: Writing 1 to bit n sets PORTx.OUT bit n, driving Pxn high; 0 does nothing. Reads return PORTx.OUT.

fields.name: OUTCLR
fields.text: Writing 1 to bit n clears PORTx.OUT bit n, driving Pxn low; 0 does nothing. Reads return PORTx.OUT.

fields.name: OUTTGL
fields.text: Writing 1 to bit n flips PORTx.OUT bit n; 0 does nothing. Reads return PORTx.OUT.

fields.name: IN
fields.text: Pin levels as sampled by the digital input buffers; a pin whose buffer is off (ISC in PORTx.PINnCTRL) is not sampled and keeps its last value. Writing 1 to bit n flips PORTx.OUT bit n; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: INT
fields.text: Bit n is set when Pxn's level or edge matches its ISC setting in PORTx.PINnCTRL; writing 1 clears it, 0 does nothing.

fields.name: INVEN
fields.text: Inverts pin n's input and output.

fields.name: PULLUPEN
fields.text: Internal pull-up on pin n while it is input only.

fields.name: ISC
fields.text: Input buffer and interrupt sense for pin n. With the buffer off, PORTx.IN bit n stops updating.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: One bit per pin: turns the pin's output driver on or off; the digital input buffer is set separately by ISC in PORTx.PINnCTRL.

fields.name: OUT
fields.text: One bit per pin: the level driven on the pin, taking effect only while PORTx.DIR has its driver on.

fields.name: IN
fields.text: One bit per pin: reads the pin's state while its digital input buffer (ISC in PORTx.PINnCTRL) is on; with the buffer off the bit is not sampled and holds. Writing 1 toggles the matching PORTx.OUT bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: INT
fields.text: One flag per pin, set when the pin's level or change matches its ISC setting in PORTx.PINnCTRL; writing 1 clears it, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SAMPFREQ
fields.text: Picks how often the BOD samples; reset value comes from SAMPFREQ in FUSE.BODCFG; not under CCP.

fields.name: ACTIVE
fields.text: BOD mode while the device is in Active or Idle; reset value comes from ACTIVE in FUSE.BODCFG; not under CCP.

values.name: ENWAKE
values.text: On, continuous; at wake-up execution waits until the BOD is running.

fields.name: SLEEP
fields.text: BOD mode while the device sleeps in Standby or Power-Down; reset value comes from SLEEP in FUSE.BODCFG.

fields.name: LVL
fields.text: Sets the BOD trip level; reset value comes from LVL in FUSE.BODCFG. Listed levels are typical.

fields.name: VLMLVL
fields.text: Places the VLM threshold a set margin above the BOD threshold (LVL in BOD.CTRLB).

fields.name: VLMCFG
fields.text: Picks which VDD crossing of the VLM threshold raises the VLM interrupt.

values.name: CROSS
values.text: VDD passes the threshold either way.

fields.name: VLMIE
fields.text: Set to 1 to turn on the VLM interrupt.

fields.name: VLMIF
fields.text: Goes high on a VLM trigger chosen by VLMCFG in BOD.INTCTRL; updates only while the BOD is on.

fields.name: VLMS
fields.text: Whether VDD is above or below the VLM threshold; meaningful only while the BOD is on.

fields.name: ADC0REFSEL
fields.text: Picks the reference voltage for ADC0.

fields.name: DAC0REFSEL
fields.text: Picks the reference voltage shared by DAC0 and AC0.

fields.name: DAC2REFEN
fields.text: 1 keeps the DAC2/AC2 reference running even when nothing asks for it; 0 lets it switch on and off as needed.

fields.name: ADC1REFEN
fields.text: 1 keeps the ADC1 reference running even when nothing asks for it; 0 lets it switch on and off as needed. Leave it 0 while ADC1 uses the external reference (REFSEL in ADC.CTRLC).

fields.name: DAC1REFEN
fields.text: 1 keeps the DAC1/AC1 reference running even when nothing asks for it; 0 lets it switch on and off as needed.

fields.name: ADC0REFEN
fields.text: 1 keeps the ADC0 reference running even when nothing asks for it; 0 lets the peripheral switch it on and off. Leave it 0 while ADC0 uses the external reference (REFSEL in ADC.CTRLC).

fields.name: DAC0REFEN
fields.text: 1 keeps the DAC0/AC0 reference running even when nothing asks for it; 0 lets the peripheral switch it on and off.

fields.name: ADC1REFSEL
fields.text: Picks the reference voltage for ADC1.

fields.name: DAC1REFSEL
fields.text: Picks the reference voltage shared by DAC1 and AC1.

fields.name: DAC2REFSEL
fields.text: Picks the reference voltage shared by DAC2 and AC2.

fields.name: WINDOW
fields.text: Any non-zero value turns on Window mode and sets how long the closed window lasts. Read-only while LOCK in WDT.STATUS is 1, writable while it is 0.

fields.name: PERIOD
fields.text: Any non-zero value turns on the WDT and sets the Normal-mode time-out; in Window mode it sets how long the open window lasts. Read-only while LOCK in WDT.STATUS is 1, writable while it is 0.

fields.name: LOCK
fields.text: Writing 1 locks WDT.CTRLA against writes; it can only be written to 1 and cleared only in Debug mode. Set by itself when PERIOD in WDT.CTRLA is non-zero after boot code. Under CCP.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: High after a write to WDT.CTRLA while the value crosses from the system clock domain into the WDT clock domain; hardware clears it when done. Not under CCP.

fields.name: CLKSEL
fields.text: Sets the timer/counter clock as a division of CLK_PER.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the timer/counter on.

fields.name: CMP2EN
fields.text: Compare channel 2 enable.

fields.name: CMP1EN
fields.text: Compare channel 1 enable.

fields.name: CMP0EN
fields.text: Compare channel 0 enable.

fields.name: ALUPD
fields.text: Lets hardware drive LUPD in TCAn.CTRLE: when 1, LUPD stays set until every enabled channel's CMPnBV is 1, then clears; at the next UPDATE the buffers move into CMPn and LUPD sets again, so no CMPnBUF value moves until all enabled buffers are written.

fields.name: WGMODE
fields.text: Selects the waveform mode, which fixes the count sequence, TOP, the UPDATE and interrupt points, and the waveform shape. Normal mode makes no waveform; in the other modes a pin gets the waveform only when its CMPnEN is set and the pin is an output. UPDATE and OVF at TOP apply when counting up.

fields.name: CMP2OV
fields.text: Compare output value for channel 2, as CMP0OV.

fields.name: CMP1OV
fields.text: Compare output value for channel 1, as CMP0OV.

fields.name: CMP0OV
fields.text: Writes the waveform generator's compare output directly while the timer/counter is not enabled, setting or clearing the WG output when it is stopped.

fields.name: SPLITM
fields.text: Puts the timer/counter in Split mode: two 8-bit timer/counters, with a changed register map.

registers.name: CTRLECLR
registers.title: Control Register E Clear - Normal Mode

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Software command to update, restart or reset the timer/counter; always reads 0.

values.name: RESET
values.text: Force a hard reset; ignored while the timer/counter is enabled.

fields.name: LUPD
fields.text: Holds back buffer transfers so all buffers can be made valid before an update happens.

values.text: Buffered registers update at each UPDATE condition.
Buffered registers do not update, even on an UPDATE condition.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Count direction; normally set by hardware from the waveform mode or event actions, and software may change it too.

registers.name: CTRLESET
registers.title: Control Register E Set - Normal Mode

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Software command to update, restart or reset the timer/counter; always reads 0.

values.name: RESET
values.text: Force a hard reset; ignored while the timer/counter is enabled.

fields.name: LUPD
fields.text: Holds back buffer transfers so all buffers can be made valid before an update happens.

values.text: Buffered registers update at each UPDATE condition.
Buffered registers do not update, even on an UPDATE condition.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Count direction; normally set by hardware from the waveform mode or event actions, and software may change it too.

fields.name: CMP2BV
fields.text: Compare 2 buffer valid, as CMP0BV.

fields.name: CMP1BV
fields.text: Compare 1 buffer valid, as CMP0BV.

fields.name: CMP0BV
fields.text: Goes high when TCAn.CMP0BUF is written; cleared by hardware at an UPDATE condition.

fields.name: PERBV
fields.text: Goes high when TCAn.PERBUF is written; cleared by hardware at an UPDATE condition.

fields.name: CMP2BV
fields.text: Compare 2 buffer valid, as CMP0BV.

fields.name: CMP1BV
fields.text: Compare 1 buffer valid, as CMP0BV.

fields.name: CMP0BV
fields.text: Goes high when TCAn.CMP0BUF is written; cleared by hardware at an UPDATE condition.

fields.name: PERBV
fields.text: Goes high when TCAn.PERBUF is written; cleared by hardware at an UPDATE condition.

fields.name: EVACT
fields.text: What the counter does in response to an event input.

values.name: EVACT_ANYEDGE
values.text: Count each event edge, rising or falling.

values.name: EVACT_HIGHLVL
values.text: Count prescaled clock cycles while the event is high.

values.name: EVACT_UPDOWN
values.text: Count prescaled clock cycles, up while the event is low and down while it is high.

fields.name: CNTEI
fields.text: Lets the event input drive counting.

values.text: Event counting on, as set by EVACT.

fields.name: CMP2
fields.text: Interrupt enable for compare channel 2, as CMP0.

fields.name: CMP1
fields.text: Interrupt enable for compare channel 1, as CMP0.

fields.name: CMP0
fields.text: Set to 1 to turn on the compare channel 0 interrupt.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Set to 1 to turn on the overflow/underflow interrupt.

fields.name: CMP2
fields.text: Interrupt flag for compare channel 2, as CMP0.

fields.name: CMP1
fields.text: Interrupt flag for compare channel 1, as CMP0.

fields.name: CMP0
fields.text: Goes high in every mode when CNT matches CMP0; stays set until a 1 is written to it.

fields.name: OVF

fields.text: Set once the whole frame has left the transmit shift register and TXDATA holds nothing new. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: DREIF
fields.text: 1 when the transmit buffer is empty and can take data, 0 while it holds data not yet moved to the shift register; 1 after reset. Writing TXDATAL clears it; always write 0 here when writing STATUS. A DRE handler must write TXDATA or disable the interrupt, or it fires again on return.

fields.name: RXSIF
fields.text: Set in Standby sleep when a valid high-to-low (idle to Start) edge is seen on RxD; reads 0 when start detection is off. Cleared only by writing 1. Unused in Master SPI mode.

fields.name: ISFIF
fields.text: Set when auto-baud is on and the measured Sync Field bit duration is out of range for a valid baud setting, or in LINAUTO mode when the SYNC character is not 0x55. Write 1 to clear it and return the USART to Idle.

fields.name: BDF
fields.text: For LINAUTO receive (and likewise GENAUTO): set after a valid break, at least 11 bit times low, and sync character; cleared by the next received data or by writing 1. Unused in NORMAL and CLK2X modes.

fields.name: WFB
fields.text: Write 1 to treat the next low-then-high transition on RxD as a break character of any width; with GENAUTO this lets BREAK and SYNC set any baud rate within the range of BAUD. Reads 0.

fields.name: RXCIE
fields.text: Enables the Receive Complete interrupt (vector RXC), raised when STATUS.RXCIF is set.

fields.name: TXCIE
fields.text: Enables the Transmit Complete interrupt (vector TXC), raised when STATUS.TXCIF is set.

fields.name: DREIE
fields.text: Enables the Data Register Empty interrupt (vector DRE), raised when STATUS.DREIF is set.

fields.name: RXSIE
fields.text: 1 lets the Start Frame Detector raise an interrupt on vector RXC when a Start-of-Frame is detected.

fields.name: LBME
fields.text: 1 connects the TXD pin internally to the receiver and cuts the RXD pin off from it.

fields.name: ABEIE
fields.text: 1 enables the auto-baud error interrupt on vector RXC, raised when ISFIF is set.

fields.name: RS485
fields.text: Turns on RS-485 and picks how. Bit 0: XDIR is driven high one clock cycle before transmission starts and low again when it ends. Bit 1: TXD becomes an output one clock cycle before transmission starts and an input again when it ends.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: 1 enables the receiver. Disabling it flushes the receive buffer, invalidating FERR, BUFOVF and PERR, and in GENAUTO and LINAUTO modes resets the auto-baud logic.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: 1 enables the transmitter, which takes over the TXD pin from the port. A 0 takes effect only after the shift register and transmit buffer have emptied; the pin is then released and made an input by hardware even if it had been set as an output.

fields.name: SFDEN
fields.text: 1 enables Start-of-Frame detection, which can wake the device from Idle or Standby sleep on a high-to-low (idle to Start) edge on RxD.

fields.name: ODME
fields.text: 1 makes TXD open-drain. The pin's pull-up (PORTx.PINnCTRL.PULLUPEN) should be on so the line does not float while sending a 1.

fields.name: RXMODE
fields.text: Receiver mode. CLK2X halves the baud divisor from 16 to 8, doubling the asynchronous rate, and has no effect in synchronous operation, where RXMODE should be 0x00; RXMODE must also be 0x00 in IRCOM mode. GENAUTO accepts any SYNC of eight alternating bits that gives a valid baud rate; LINAUTO requires every two bits to fall within 32 ±6 baud samples of the internal rate and the value 0x55. GENAUTO and LINAUTO work only in Asynchronous Slave mode.

fields.name: MPCM
fields.text: 1 enables Multi-Processor Communication mode: the receiver drops every frame that carries no address information. The transmitter is not affected.

fields.name: CMODE
fields.text: Communication mode. Writing 0x03 (MSPI) changes which fields this register holds.

fields.name: PMODE
fields.text: Turns parity on and picks its type. The transmitter adds a parity bit to each frame; the receiver computes parity of incoming data, compares it to this setting and sets STATUS.PERR on a mismatch.

fields.name: SBMODE
fields.text: Number of Stop bits the transmitter sends; the receiver does not use it.

fields.name: CHSIZE
fields.text: Data bits per frame, shared by receiver and transmitter. For 9-bit characters the order of low and high byte access to RXDATA and TXDATA can be chosen.

values.name: 9BITL
values.text: Nine bits, low byte accessed first.

values.name: 9BITH
values.text: Nine bits, high byte accessed first.

fields.name: CMODE
fields.text: Communication mode. Writing anything other than 0x03 (MSPI) changes which fields this register holds.

fields.name: UDORD
fields.text: Bit order of a frame, shared by receiver and transmitter. Changing it corrupts any transfer in progress in either direction.

fields.name: UCPHA
fields.text: Picks whether data is sampled on the leading (first) or trailing (last) edge of XCK.

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: 16-bit baud rate setting, low byte at the register's offset and high byte one above. A write updates the baud prescaler at once; changing it corrupts transfers in progress.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Debug run: whether the USART keeps running while the CPU is halted in Break Debug mode.

values.text: Halted in Break Debug mode, events ignored.
Keeps running while the CPU is halted in Break Debug mode.

fields.name: IREI
fields.text: Enables the event input as the IRCOM receiver source; when selected, the RXD pin input is cut off automatically.

registers.name: TXPLCTRL
registers.title: IRCOM Transmitter Pulse Length Control Register

fields.name: TXPL
fields.text: Transmitter pulse modulation scheme. Takes effect only in IRCOM mode and must be set before TXEN. With fixed pulse length, each pulse begins in step with the baud clock's rising edge. 0xFF turns pulse coding off so RX and TX pass through the IRCOM module unchanged, which allows half-duplex USART, loop-back testing and RX input from an event channel.

values.text: Pulses of 3/16 of the baud period.
Fixed pulse length; the value is the pulse width in system clock periods.

registers.name: RXPLCTRL
registers.title: IRCOM Receiver Pulse Length Control Register

fields.name: RXPL
fields.text: Filter coefficient of the IRCOM receiver. Takes effect only in IRCOM mode and must be set before RXEN.

values.text: Filtering on; RXPL+1 samples are needed to accept a received pulse.

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Data order: which end of the data word goes out first.

fields.name: MASTER
fields.text: Selects master or slave. If SS is an input and is pulled low while this is 1, the bit clears and INTFLAGS.IF sets; write 1 again to return to master. CTRLB.SSD governs this behaviour.

fields.name: CLK2X
fields.text: 1 doubles the SCK frequency after the prescaler, in Master mode.

fields.name: PRESC
fields.text: SCK rate in Master mode as a fraction of CLK_PER; no effect in Slave mode. CLK2X doubles the result.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the SPI on.

fields.name: BUFEN
fields.text: 1 enables Buffer mode: two receive buffers and one transmit buffer, with separate transmit complete and receive complete flags.

fields.name: BUFWR
fields.text: Buffer mode wait for receive. With 0, the first byte transferred is a dummy.

values.text: Data is copied into the shift register only after one transfer has completed.
With the SPI enabled and SS high, the first write to DATA goes straight into the shift register.

fields.name: SSD
fields.text: When set in master operation (CTRLA.MASTER = 1), SS no longer takes the SPI out of Master mode.

values.text: SS line in use as master.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Transfer mode: SCK polarity and phase. Sets whether the leading clock edge rises or falls and whether data is set up and sampled on the leading or trailing edge. A rising leading edge means SCK idles low; a falling one means it idles high.

values.text: Rising leading edge samples, falling trailing edge sets up.
Rising leading edge sets up, falling trailing edge samples.
Falling leading edge samples, rising trailing edge sets up.
Falling leading edge sets up, rising trailing edge samples.

fields.name: RXCIE
fields.text: Buffer mode only: enables the Receive Complete interrupt, raised when INTFLAGS.RXCIF sets. Reads 0 outside Buffer mode.

fields.name: TXCIE
fields.text: Buffer mode only: enables the Transfer Complete interrupt, raised when INTFLAGS.TXCIF sets. Reads 0 outside Buffer mode.

fields.name: DREIE
fields.text: Buffer mode only: enables the Data Register Empty interrupt, raised when INTFLAGS.DREIF sets. Reads 0 outside Buffer mode.

fields.name: SSIE
fields.text: Buffer mode only: enables the Slave Select interrupt, raised when INTFLAGS.SSIF sets. Reads 0 outside Buffer mode.

fields.name: IE
fields.text: Enables the SPI interrupt outside Buffer mode, raised when INTFLAGS.RXCIF/IF sets.

fields.name: IF
fields.text: Set when a transfer completes and a whole byte has shifted through DATA, and also when SS is an input pulled low in Master mode. Cleared by hardware when its interrupt vector runs, or by reading INTFLAGS while it is set and then accessing DATA.

fields.name: WRCOL
fields.text: Set when DATA is written before the current byte has finished shifting out. Cleared by reading INTFLAGS while it is set and then accessing DATA.

fields.name: RXCIF
fields.text: Set while the receive data buffer holds unread data, cleared when it is empty or by writing 1. With interrupt-driven reception the handler has to read DATA to clear it, or the interrupt fires again on return.

fields.name: TXCIF
fields.text: Set when the transmit shift register has emptied and DATA holds nothing new. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: DREIF
fields.text: 1 when the transmit buffer is empty and can take data, 0 while it holds data not yet moved to the shift register. Cleared after reset and by writing DATA. A DRE handler must write DATA or disable the interrupt, or it fires again on return.

fields.name: SSIF
fields.text: Set when the SPI was a master and SS was pulled low externally, so it now runs as a slave; set only if CTRLB.SSD is not 1. Write 1 to clear.

fields.name: BUFOVF
fields.text: Set when data was lost: the two-byte receive buffer was full and a third byte arrived in the shift register. Without transmit data it is not set before a new transfer starts. Cleared by reading DATA or writing 1.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Send and receive data. A write starts a transfer in Master mode and readies the byte to send in Slave mode. Not a physical register: in Normal mode a write goes to the shift register and a read comes from the receive data register; in Buffer mode a write goes to the transmit data buffer and a read comes from the receive data buffer, after which the receive data register moves into that buffer.

fields.name: SDASETUP
fields.text: Setup time on SDA out while the TWI slave is being read; four clock cycles by default.

fields.name: SDAHOLD
fields.text: SDA hold time.

fields.name: FMPEN
fields.text: 1 selects 1 MHz bus speed (Fast mode Plus) in the default configuration.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Debug run: whether the TWI keeps running while the CPU is halted in Break Debug mode.

values.text: Halted in Break Debug mode, events ignored.
Keeps running while the CPU is halted in Break Debug mode.

fields.name: RIEN
fields.text: 1 enables the master read interrupt on MSTATUS.RIF; the interrupt also needs CPU.SREG.I set.

fields.name: WIEN
fields.text: 1 enables the master write interrupt on MSTATUS.WIF; the interrupt also needs CPU.SREG.I set.

fields.name: QCEN
fields.text: 1 enables Quick Command mode: when a slave acknowledges the address, RIF or WIF sets according to the R/W bit, and software must then write a Stop command to MCTRLB.MCMD.

fields.name: TIMEOUT
fields.text: Inactive bus time-out; any nonzero value enables it, and a bus idle longer than the setting puts the bus state logic in Idle.

values.name: 50US
values.text: 50 µs (SMBus), at a 100 kHz baud rate.

values.name: 100US
values.text: 100 µs, at a 100 kHz baud rate.

values.name: 200US
values.text: 200 µs, at a 100 kHz baud rate.

fields.name: SMEN
fields.text: 1 enables master Smart mode: the MCTRLB.ACKACT value is sent as soon as MDATA is read.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: 1 turns on the TWI master.

fields.name: FLUSH
fields.text: Writing 1 pulses for one clock cycle, disabling and re-enabling the master, which clears its internal state and sets the bus state to Idle. Writing 0 does nothing. Writing MDATA before MADDR makes the TWI send invalid data.

fields.name: ACKACT
fields.text: Acknowledge the master sends. With MCTRLA.SMEN = 1 it is sent when MDATA is read; otherwise a command has to be written to MCMD. Not sent when MDATA is written.

fields.name: MCMD
fields.text: Strobe that starts a master operation; reads 0. 0x0 NOACT: reserved. 0x1 REPSTART: acknowledge action, then repeated Start. 0x2 RECVTRANS: acknowledge action, then a byte read (when reading) or no action and a byte write (when writing). 0x3 STOP: acknowledge action, then Stop. ACKACT can be written together with MCMD; on a master write the TWI waits for new data in MDATA.

rows: Acknowledge action, then a repeated Start.
Acknowledge action, then a byte read (read); no acknowledge action, then a byte write (write).

fields.name: RIF
fields.text: Set when a master byte read completes successfully; drives the master read interrupt (MCTRLA.RIEN). Cleared by writing 1, writing MADDR, writing or reading MDATA, or writing MCTRLB.MCMD.

fields.name: WIF
fields.text: Set when a master address or byte write completes, even after a bus error or lost arbitration; drives the master write interrupt (MCTRLA.WIEN). Cleared the same ways as RIF.

fields.name: CLKHOLD
fields.text: Reads 1 while the master holds SCL low, stretching the clock. Cleared the same ways as RIF.

fields.name: RXACK
fields.text: Last acknowledge from the slave: 0 for ACK, the slave ready for more; 1 for NACK, the slave unable or not needing to take more.

fields.name: ARBLOST
fields.text: Reads 1 when the master lost arbitration, while sending a high data bit, a NACK, a Start or a repeated Start. Cleared the same ways as RIF.

fields.name: BUSERR
fields.text: Set on an illegal bus operation: a Start, repeated Start or Stop that breaks the protocol, such as a Start followed directly by a Stop. Cleared by writing 1 or writing MADDR. Detection needs the master enabled (MCTRLA.ENABLE = 1) and a main clock at least four times SCL.

fields.name: BUSSTATE
fields.text: Current bus state.

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Sets the SCL high and low times. Write it only while the master is off (MCTRLA.ENABLE = 0).

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Slave address to contact; bit 0 is the R/W direction. A write makes the TWI issue a Start and send the byte, depending on bus state; a read can be done at any time without disturbing the bus.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Direct access to the master shift register, so it cannot be used during a byte transfer; valid access needs CLKHOLD read as 1 or an interrupt. A write sends a byte and then takes the slave's acknowledge, whatever ACKACT is, and completes even if arbitration is lost before WIF sets. With MCTRLA.SMEN = 1 a read makes the master perform the ACKACT acknowledge action. Reading with ACKACT = 1 clears WIF and RIF; ARBLOST and BUSERR are not changed.

fields.name: DIEN
fields.text: 1 enables the slave data interrupt on SSTATUS.DIF; it fires only when this bit, DIF and CPU.SREG.I are all 1.

fields.name: APIEN
fields.text: 1 enables the slave address or stop interrupt on SSTATUS.APIF; it fires only when this bit, APIF and CPU.SREG.I are all 1. Address and Stop share the flag and vector; APIF is set on Stop only with PIEN = 1, and SSTATUS.AP tells which caused it.

fields.name: PIEN
fields.text: 1 lets a Stop condition set SSTATUS.APIF. Needs a main clock at least four times SCL.

fields.name: PMEN
fields.text: 1: the slave answers every address. 0: it answers the address in SADDR.

fields.name: SMEN
fields.text: 1 enables slave Smart mode: writing SCTRLB.SCMD or accessing SDATA clears the interrupt and the transfer goes on. With it off, the slave always waits for a new command.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: 1 turns on the TWI slave.

fields.name: ACKACT
fields.text: Acknowledge the slave sends. With SCTRLA.SMEN = 1 it is sent when SDATA is read; otherwise a command has to be written to SCMD. Not sent when SDATA is written.

fields.name: SCMD
fields.text: Strobe that starts a slave operation; reads 0. 0x0 NOACT: nothing. 0x1: reserved. 0x2 COMPTRANS, ending a transaction: when writing, acknowledge action then wait for any Start; when reading, wait for any Start. 0x3 RESPONSE: after an address interrupt (APIF), acknowledge action then the next byte received (write) or a data interrupt (read); after a data interrupt (DIF), acknowledge action then the next byte received (write) or a byte read followed by the acknowledge action (read). ACKACT can be written with SCMD and updates before the command runs.

rows: Ends a transaction: on a write, acknowledge action, then wait for any Start (S/Sr); on a read, wait for any Start (S/Sr).

After an address interrupt (APIF): acknowledge action, then the next byte received (write) or a slave data interrupt (read). After a data interrupt (DIF): acknowledge action, then the next byte received (write), or a byte read, then the acknowledge action (read).

fields.name: DIF
fields.text: Set when a slave byte transmit or receive finishes without bus error; can also set on a failed transfer after a collision (COLL). Drives the slave data interrupt (SCTRLA.DIEN). Cleared by writing or reading SDATA or writing SCTRLB.SCMD.

fields.name: APIF
fields.text: Set when the slave's address is received or on a Stop condition; drives the slave address or stop interrupt (SCTRLA.APIEN). Cleared the same ways as DIF.

fields.name: CLKHOLD
fields.text: Reads 1 while the slave holds SCL low, stretching the clock. Set by an address or data interrupt and cleared when that interrupt is cleared.

fields.name: RXACK
fields.text: Last acknowledge from the master: 0 for ACK, 1 for NACK.

fields.name: COLL
fields.text: Reads 1 when the slave could not drive high bits on SDA (DIF then sets as the failed transfer ends) or could not send a NACK (because the address had already matched and APIF set). Cleared by writing 1 or by any Start. COLL has no interrupt of its own; the APIF and DIF interrupt handlers are where it can be checked.

fields.name: BUSERR
fields.text: Set on an illegal bus operation: a Start, repeated Start or Stop that breaks the protocol, such as a Start followed directly by a Stop. Write 1 to clear. Detection lives in the master, so the slave sees it only with the master enabled (MCTRLA.ENABLE = 1) and a main clock at least four times SCL.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: Bus direction from the R/W bit of the last address received: 1 for a master read in progress, 0 for a master write.

fields.name: AP
fields.text: When APIF is set, tells whether an address match or a Stop caused it.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Slave address the address match logic compares against: ADDR[7:1] is the main address; ADDR[0] = 1 enables recognition of the I2C General Call address 0x00. An address packet received sets SSTATUS.APIF and SSTATUS.AP.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: Slave data register. Access is valid only while the slave holds SCL low (CLKHOLD = 1); software that tracks the protocol through interrupts or flags need not check CLKHOLD first. With SCTRLA.SMEN = 1, a read during clock hold starts bus operations and makes the slave perform the SCTRLB.ACKACT acknowledge action.

fields.name: ADDRMASK
fields.text: With ADDREN = 0, a 7-bit mask on SADDR: each 1 makes the matching address bit always match, so a range of addresses is recognised. With ADDREN = 1, a second slave address alongside SADDR.

fields.name: ADDREN
fields.text: 0: SADDRMASK masks SADDR. 1: the slave answers both SADDR and SADDRMASK as separate addresses.

registers.name: CTRLA
registers.title: Control A
notes: Not writable after an NMI has been triggered.

fields.name: RESET
fields.text: Strobe: 1 resets CRCSCAN, clearing CTRLA, CTRLB and STATUS one clock cycle later. With NMIEN = 0 it can be written busy or not and acts at once; with NMIEN = 1 only while STATUS.BUSY is 0.

fields.name: NMIEN
fields.text: 1 makes any CRC failure raise an NMI. Can be set only while STATUS.BUSY is 0, and cleared only by a system reset, not by RESET.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: 1 enables CRCSCAN with the current settings and starts a check; it stays 1 after the check, and writing 1 again starts another. Writing 0 does nothing. If a scan at start-up is configured, it reads 1 when code begins to run. STATUS.BUSY shows a check in progress.

registers.name: CTRLB
registers.title: Control B
notes: Not writable while the CRC is busy or after an NMI has been triggered.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Flash access mode. If the CRC ran during reset initialization, MODE reads nonzero when code starts; write it to 0x0 again for correct operation under code execution.

values.name: PRIORITY
values.text: One check with priority to Flash; the CPU halts until it finishes.

fields.name: SRC
fields.text: Flash section to check; section sizes come from fuses. If the CRC ran during reset initialization, SRC reads FLASH, BOOTAPP or BOOT when code starts, per that configuration.

values.name: FLASH
values.text: Whole Flash: boot, application code and application data.

fields.name: OK
fields.text: 1 when the last CRC passed; 1 by default before any scan. Valid only with BUSY at 0.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: 1 while a check is running; access to the control registers is limited meanwhile.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Whether CLK_PER keeps running in Standby sleep; ignored where CLK_PER is not needed.

values.text: Standby does not need the system clock.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the CCL on.

fields.name: SEQSEL
fields.text: Sequential element for the LUT0 and LUT1 pair.

fields.name: EDGEDET
fields.text: Edge detection on the LUT.

fields.name: CLKSRC
fields.text: Clock (CLK_MUX_OUT) for the LUT: CLK_PER or the signal on IN[2]. The even LUT's clock drives the sequential block of the pair.

fields.name: FILTSEL
fields.text: Filter on the LUT output.

fields.name: OUTEN
fields.text: 1 drives the LUT output onto the LUTnOUT pin, overriding the port's pin setting.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the LUT on.

registers.name: LUTCTRLB
registers.title: LUT n Control B
notes: SPI inputs to the CCL work only with the SPI as master; USART inputs only in asynchronous or synchronous USART master mode.

fields.name: INSEL1
fields.text: Source of input 1 of the LUT.

fields.name: INSEL0
fields.text: Source of input 0 of the LUT.

fields.name: INSEL2
fields.text: Source of input 2 of the LUT.

fields.name: TRUTH
fields.text: Truth table: the LUT output for each combination of inputs IN[2:0].

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: When 1, the AC keeps running in Standby sleep mode; with the clock stopped there, interrupts and status flags do not update.

values.text: Keeps running in Standby sleep mode.

fields.name: OUTEN
fields.text: When 1, the OUT signal is driven onto its pin.

fields.name: INTMODE
fields.text: Picks which edges of the AC output raise an interrupt request.

fields.name: LPMODE
fields.text: When 1, the comparator runs on less current: lower power, slower response.

fields.name: HYSMODE
fields.text: Picks the hysteresis applied at the AC input.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the AC on when 1.

fields.name: INVERT
fields.text: When 1, the AC output is inverted, for every peripheral fed by it and for the internal status signals.

fields.name: MUXPOS
fields.text: Chooses the signal on the AC positive input; low pin-count packages lack some port pins.

fields.name: MUXNEG
fields.text: Chooses the signal on the AC negative input; low pin-count packages lack some port pins.

values.name: DAC
values.text: DAC output; ACn takes DACn (AC0 with DAC0, AC1 with DAC1).

fields.name: CMP
fields.text: Turns on the comparator interrupt when 1.

fields.name: STATE
fields.text: Reads the present level of the AC OUT signal, lagging by a three-cycle synchronizer.

fields.name: CMP
fields.text: The AC interrupt flag; write 1 to clear it.

fields.name: RUNSTBY
fields.text: Sets whether the ADC keeps running while the chip is in Standby sleep mode.

fields.name: RESSEL
fields.text: Picks the conversion resolution.

values.text: 10 bits; full 10-bit results go into ADC.RES or the accumulator.
8 bits; each result keeps its eight upper bits, losing the two lowest, before it is stored in ADC.RES or accumulated.

fields.name: FREERUN
fields.text: When 1, conversions repeat back to back: writing ADC.COMMAND.STCONV to 1 starts the first, and each new one begins as the last finishes, marked by ADCn.INTFLAGS.RESRDY.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: ADC Enable.

fields.name: SAMPNUM
fields.text: Number of back-to-back samples summed automatically into ADC.RES for one complete conversion; above 0x0 the sum is taken.

fields.name: SAMPCAP
fields.text: Selects the sampling capacitance, which sets the input impedance; the right choice depends on the reference voltage and the circuit around the input.

fields.name: REFSEL
fields.text: Chooses the ADC voltage reference.

fields.name: PRESC
fields.text: Divider from CLK_PER down to CLK_ADC.

fields.name: INITDLY
fields.text: Start-up wait, in CLK_ADC cycles, before the first sample after the ADC is enabled, after a switch to an internal reference, or on wake from deep sleep for a measurement, so the reference and MUXes have settled.

fields.name: ASDV
fields.text: When 1, SAMPDLY steps up by one after every sample, wrapping from 0xF to 0x0, so the sampling instant moves around and steady tones in the spectrum are avoided.

fields.name: SAMPDLY
fields.text: Extra wait between consecutive samples, equal to the field value in CLK_ADC cycles, with the sampling capacitor held open; varying it shifts the sampling rate during hardware accumulation to reject periodic noise, and ASDV can step it automatically.

fields.name: WINCM
fields.text: Turns on Window Comparator mode and picks the condition that sets the flag, comparing the 16-bit accumulated RESULT with the 16-bit thresholds WINLT (low) and WINHT (high).

values.name: NONE
values.text: No window comparison; the reset setting.

values.name: OUTSIDE
values.text: RESULT under WINLT or over WINHT.

fields.name: SAMPLEN
fields.text: Adds CLK_ADC cycles to the sampling time, which is two CLK_ADC cycles by default; longer sampling suits higher-impedance sources and lengthens each conversion.

fields.name: MUXPOS
fields.text: Chooses the single-ended input routed to the ADC; a change made mid-conversion applies once that conversion ends. Low pin-count packages lack some port pins.

values.name: PTC
values.text: Reserved on ADC0; DAC2 on ADC1.

values.name: INTREF
values.text: Internal reference from the VREF peripheral.

values.name: TEMPSENSE
values.text: Temperature sensor on ADC0; DAC1 on ADC1.

fields.name: STCONV
fields.text: Write 1 to start one conversion, or the first one in Free-Running mode; reads 1 while a conversion runs and clears itself when it finishes.

fields.name: STARTEI
fields.text: Lets the event input start a conversion.

fields.name: WCMP
fields.text: Turns on the window comparator interrupt when 1.

fields.name: RESRDY
fields.text: Turns on the result ready interrupt when 1.

fields.name: WCMP
fields.text: Set at the end of a conversion whose result meets the condition chosen by ADCn.CTRLE.WINCM; cleared by writing 1 or by reading ADCn.RES. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RESRDY
fields.text: Set when a conversion finishes and a new result is waiting; cleared by writing 1 or by reading ADCn.RES. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Debug Run.

values.text: Stops in Break Debug mode and ignores events.
Keeps running in Break Debug mode while the CPU is halted.

fields.name: TEMP
fields.text: Holding byte used when reading or writing this peripheral's 16-bit registers.

registers.name: RES
registers.title: Result
notes: An input above the reference gives the 10-bit maximum 0x3FF; an input below 0 V gives 0x000.
The accumulated result never exceeds 0xFFC0, even after 64 accumulations.

fields.name: RES
fields.text: The conversion or accumulated result, RES[15] its top bit; the converter itself gives 10 bits, ADC[9:0], ADC[9] on top. Values are 1's complement: 0x0000 is zero and 0xFFFF is full scale.

registers.name: WINLT
registers.title: Window Comparator Low Threshold
notes: When samples are accumulated, the thresholds are compared with the accumulated value, not with each sample.

fields.name: WINLT
fields.text: The 16-bit low threshold of the window comparator.

fields.name: WINHT
fields.text: The 16-bit high threshold of the window comparator.

fields.name: DUTYCYC
fields.text: Sets the duty cycle of the ADC clock; an ADC clock above 1.5 MHz needs at least 2.7 V supply.

values.text: 50 % duty cycle; required above 1.5 MHz ADC clock.
25 % duty cycle (25 % high, 75 % low); required at 1.5 MHz ADC clock or below.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: When 1, the DAC or its output buffer is not switched off automatically when the device enters Standby sleep mode.

fields.name: OUTEN
fields.text: When 1, the output buffer is on and drives OUT onto a pin.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the DAC on when 1.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: The digital value the DAC turns into an output voltage.

fields.name: UPDIREV
fields.text: Revision number of this UPDI.

fields.name: PESIG
fields.text: Code of the last internal UPDI error; a debugger read clears it.

rows: The access layer returned no data or response to the UPDI.
Drive contention seen on the UPDI pin.

fields.name: IBDLY
fields.text: When 1, the UPDI inserts a fixed gap of two IDLE bits between the data bytes it sends during multi-byte LD(S).

fields.name: PARD
fields.text: When 1, the UPDI ignores the parity bit and does no parity checking; recommended for testing only.

fields.name: DTD
fields.text: When 1, the PHY layer stops timing out on the ACC layer, which otherwise must answer within 65536 UPDI clock cycles.

fields.name: RSD
fields.text: When 1, the UPDI sends no response signatures, cutting protocol overhead for large NVM writes; this is safe only if system bus access delays are predictable, otherwise data may be lost.

fields.name: GTVAL
fields.text: Guard time the UPDI waits when it turns from receiving to sending.

fields.name: NACKDIS
fields.text: When 1, the UPDI does not send its NACK signature when a System Reset arrives during LD(S) or ST(S) operations.

fields.name: CCDETDIS
fields.text: Contention detection: 1 turns it off, 0 turns it on.

fields.name: UPDIDIS
fields.text: Write 1 to shut down the UPDI PHY interface: its clock request drops, it resets, and all PHY settings and keys are cleared.

fields.name: UROWWRITE
fields.text: Reads 1 once the UROWWRITE key is accepted; must be written as the last step of a user row write so the programming session resets properly.

fields.name: NVMPROG
fields.text: Reads 1 once the NVMPROG key is accepted; clears when NVM programming begins and ASI_SYS_STATUS.NVMPROG sets.

fields.name: CHIPERASE
fields.text: Reads 1 once the Chip Erase key is accepted; cleared by the reset request that the Chip Erase sequence issues.

fields.name: RSTREQ
fields.text: Write the reset signature to reset the system; the UPDI itself is not reset by it.

fields.name: UPDICLKSEL
fields.text: Chooses the UPDI clock frequency, 4 MHz after reset and enable; faster settings are advised only with the BOD at its highest level, 4 MHz for any other BOD level.

fields.name: UROWWRITE_FINAL
fields.text: Write 1 once the user row data is in RAM to start programming it into Flash; written early, the CPU carries on without the data. Writable only after the USERROW-Write key is accepted.

fields.name: CLKREQ
fields.text: When 1, the ASI holds a request for the system clock whatever the sleep mode, so the UPDI can reach the ACC layer while the system sleeps; 0 drops the request. Cleared when the UPDI is disabled; set by default each time the UPDI is turned on, by fuse or by high voltage.

fields.name: RSTSYS
fields.text: Reads 1 while the system domain is held in reset, 0 when it is not; clears to 0 when read. A reset held through ASI_RESET_REQ also shows here.

fields.name: INSLEEP
fields.text: Reads 1 while the system domain is in Idle or a deeper sleep mode, 0 when it is awake.

fields.name: NVMPROG
fields.text: Reads 1 when the UPDI may begin NVM programming; once finished, the UPDI has to reset the system by way of the UPDI reset register.

fields.name: UROWPROG
fields.text: Reads 1 when the UPDI may begin user row programming; once the user row data is in RAM, the UROWDONE bit of ASI_SYS_CTRLA must be written.

fields.name: LOCKSTATUS
fields.text: Reads 1 while the device is locked; reads 0 after a chip erase with the lock bits cleared.

fields.name: CRC_STATUS
fields.text: State of the CRC check, one-hot coded.
